Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: You go through it, because he throws in your mind about he owns you and the contract he’s got on you. You don’t know how they negotiate those contracts and things. You don’t know, because I never did know just what it was, and when I found out, it was too late.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Too late, because you were contractually obligated. You had no legal advice at that time? You had no lawyer?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No. I had no legal contact or person that would work for me. It was because of him. They knew him so well. Lawyers and everything knew him so well, they didn’t want to be bothered. If you were related with him . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I’m not going to give you any legal advice, because I don’t want to mess with him.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Right.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: That was their attitude.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: They didn’t want to handle – do anything for any of the artists that he was handling. That’s why I say, poor Maybelle. I know she had a rough time with . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Let’s talk about a couple of those artists in that period that you hooked up with, like Big Maybelle and Little Esther.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Larry Darnell. Remember that one? Larry Darnell was one of his hits.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Tell me a little bit about your relationship with Big Maybelle, because the idea . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Maybelle and I both came from Cleveland, and we worked around together before he even got to know her.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I see.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: We worked various cities and other clubs. She was like a little sister to me. [?]. She just had a bad situation, like myself. I didn’t have anyone handling the business for me, and Maybelle didn’t have any. She had a boyfriend that she went with. He wasn’t

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: doing anything right for her. He was letting her get that junk. I always felt that was a rough thing for her. Then she was big and fat and then using that dope. Hey. It wasn’t going to be too long. That’s what happened.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: But she was your close personal friend, and you loved hanging out with her.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Oh yeah. She’s my girl, yes.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Also, before I forget, the other character that you hooked up with in the 1950s and the early 1960s, I guess, was Little Willie John, who – I always love Little Jimmy Scott and Little Willie John, and the two of you guys together.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: We used to hang out together.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Oh you did? How did you meet?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: He wanted me to teach him all my songs.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: That’s what I was going to ask you. He wanted to be a balladeer.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Then I didn’t get around to doing that. I didn’t get around to doing that, and he sort of acted mad towards me, because I wouldn’t do it, but that’s Little Willie John, selfish.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Let me ask you something about that, because what I’ve always heard about Little Willie John – a lot of people think was one of the best rhythm-and-blues vocalists ever, along with Clyde McPhatter . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: And there would have been Lubinsky’s bet for a hit . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: If Herman . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . the kind of hit they wanted. Willie John would have been the thing.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: That’s right.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: But they never got around to . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: He was over there in King Records with . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: King Records, yeah.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . Sid Nathan.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: And he’d never got around to dealing with Lubinsky.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Let me ask you this about you and your life – this is such a – whatever was heard about Little Willie John is that he had a short man’s complex.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: That you couldn’t tell him nothing.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No, baby.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: He’d take on the big . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Willie was a little short guy, and he wanted to be a gangster. His style was . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Gangster style.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . gangster style. He thought he could be a gangster. That’s what hurt him. He’d get around people, and they didn’t want to bother with it, because he didn’t know how to talk to people.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: But in terms of you – do you ever feel like you had a short man’s complex?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Huh?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Do you feel like you ever had a short man’s complex the way Little Willie John did?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No, no. I never thought of that.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Back to mom. Accept it.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No, I never thought of myself being short or physically inadequate or whatever. But like I said, them guys, everybody wanted to be a big shot, and the kind of big shot they wanted to be was no good, because they wanted to be tough and bossy and run the show that they were involved in.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So, this period of your recordings in the 1950s, both with Royal and Savoy, you never got any royalties for that stuff?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Never got paid.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Would you . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: The most – sometimes now, I wondered [sic: remembered], he would send – Freddie Mendel[sohn] would send over a $5,000 check. This was supposed to be an advance for doing the record. I said okay. But I knew at the end of the session, he hadn’t paid the session cost. Never paid it. He did that to a whole lot of people, not only myself. I don’t feel like I was the only one that he did these things to, because I know, the more I was with him, I realized he was mistreating everybody.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: The same, equally as bad.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yes.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Equal mistreatment for everybody.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: That was just his way of living and dealing with people. He didn’t respect anything you could do. It had to be Lubinsky’s way.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Just kind of moving on a little bit here: tell us how we get into this next period of your music, that you meet Ray Charles. Did you meet him through Mary Ann?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Or had you known him before?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No, no. What it was, I had . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: This was like 1958, 1959-ish, end of the ’50s.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah. You see, we all traveled. They were travelling too. We’d meet up in different towns, and I got to know Ray. Then he got Adams – Joe Adams . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah, became his manager.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . became – he gave him a job as his manager.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Right, early 1960s now.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Uh-huh. Anyway, then he told Joe to have me come to California. He wanted to record me.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Before that, did you know that Ray was a Jimmy Scott enthusiast, a fan of yours?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No, I didn’t.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So all the times you’re hanging out, the times that you had met him on . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Right.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . the road, he never told you, “Man, I love the way you sing.” You just didn’t have any idea.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Oh. He respected me, and I always found him to be a very generous person. With all the artists that he dealt with, he was a generous person.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So you get a call from Joe Adams that says, Ray wants you to come to California.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: That I – that Ray wants to record me.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So you go to California.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I go to California. We started rehearsing at his house.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Were you instrumental – a bad pun – did you help pick out the tunes?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Oh yeah. He was glad that I wanted to do those tunes. He had intended that we would continue. He passed before we could get together.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: But, just keep it on this little time zone, for a while. So this is really, if we look at the big recording career of Jimmy Scott, beginning with Everybody’s Somebody’s Fool and Roost and Savoy . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah, I finally get . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: This is the first time . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . you got – someone was telling you, you tell me what you want to sing.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: That’s right.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: You bring me some songs.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: And allowed me to pick tunes.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: That were close to your heart.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yes.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: And where you liked the stories.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: And we were beginning to make a list, he and I. I picked tunes. He said, “I know that.” He said, “That’s beautiful, man.” “Okay, we’re going to do that.” Write it down.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: What about the orchestrators, Gerald Wilson and Marty Paich? Did they come in and work with you before the recording began? Or did Ray just tell them, okay, y’all do the charts of these songs? Do you have any recollection of working with Gerald Wilson or Marty Paich?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah, but I – it was a very short time.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So the charts got written in a hurry.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Right.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: You go up to the RPM studio on Washington Boulevard, Ray’s own studio. Did you know he was going to play piano on every track?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So that must have made you happy.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Oh yes. That was beautiful. I felt like a king.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Right. Ray’s on the track.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yes. Ray Charles is playing for me.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Every track. Let me ask you this . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: That was a big boost . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: A big boost.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . for me.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Let me ask you this, because Ray is well known as being a controlling guy in the studio: do you feel like he produced your vocals or he kind of left you . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: He left me . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . to develop your own . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . to be free . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: To be free. All right.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . and sing.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So he wasn’t telling you, “Aw man, you’re too behind the beat. Let’s move it like this”?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No, he never, never . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: “Let’s redo this, because I don’t like the way you enunciate.”

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No. He’d say, “Hey man, we will do” such and such a thing today, and we’d sit down and rehearse that song that we were going to do. After we would rehearse two or three songs, he’d go in the studio.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Was there much punching in and punching out of those vocals? In other words, were they highly edited? Or did you mainly sing them down one time or two times?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: They weren’t highly edited. Most of them were one time. It was what he wanted. At least he said he did. And we’ll do such and such a thing tomorrow, he would say to me. I’d say, “Okay,” . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So here . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . because it was pleasant, the numbers and the songs that he was projecting to me.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So here . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: They were close to the ones I wanted to sing.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah. So you’re a happy guy. So here comes the first, in your mind . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yes.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . great Jimmy Scott album that expresses your heart and your soul and your artistry . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yes, right.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . in a way that makes you happy . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Right.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . not only because you’ve got him playing behind you. You’ve got these beautiful orchestrations.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Right. And I’ve got to tell you something about that.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Please. We want to hear it.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I got to tell.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I want to hear it.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Listen. What’s his name? Tony or something?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Tony Gumina. The cat who lives down the street here? In Vegas?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Has he been to see you?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah. I know Tony well.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: You know the program he’s after.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Good. Okay. I just wanted to make sure . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I’m behind it.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . you knew, because . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No. I talk to him all the time. No, Tony wants to help you, and I want to help Tony help you, and blah blah.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Anyway, getting back to the – right, please God – getting back to the thing about – right – so, the album’s done. Ray let you be need to be and who you are. The orchestrations are beautiful. The tunes are all the songs that are of your heart songs.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yes. Of my heart.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Now, the first that happens, that a cover of the album comes out, and there’s not your picture on it. There’s a male model on the cover. What was your reaction when the album came out and your picture wasn’t on it. Did that . . . ?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Oh that. He . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Joe Adams.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: He was a no-time tap dancer.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Oh, the model.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: The man that – yeah, that was on that album.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: That’s interesting.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: And the girl – I don’t know who the girl was.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: She was probably a model too.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Probably a model or [?].

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Did that hurt you?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Huh?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Did that hurt you, when you saw a Jimmy Scott album?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So you didn’t care.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No. I was so glad that Ray was playing with me. I never thought of those things, about who was who.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: When did you first learn that there was trouble with the album from a legal point of view?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Lubinsky interferred.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Why?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: He told Ray – he even threatened the boy. He said, “I’ll have you put in jail for life.” He said, “Because that’s my artist that you recorded.” He kept threatening, calling him, threatening him. So of course, I didn’t feel bad when Ray stopped the record. He stopped the record to protect hisself. I can understand that, and I took it like that, that Ray stopped the record and put it on the shelf until he could get a clearance.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: But the other thing that always blows my mind about this story is that – so you’re in L.A., and it looks like you’ll be in L.A. to stay, because you really like L.A. . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Oh yeah. Loved it.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . and there’s more opportunities there for show business and . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yes, but the biggest – the big thing was I had – went home to Cleveland, and my father wanted to come with me back to L.A. So I put him – he got in the car and got his little suitcase, the things he wanted, and we – I drove him back to L.A. with me. We had an apartment already. So there was no problem about a bedroom for him. So he stayed with us, Mary Ann and I. I had met her, and we started going together.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Mary Ann, who was one of the original Ray Charles . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: One of the – yes, the vocalists.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . vocalists, before the Raylettes. Mary Ann Fisher.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: The song – he wrote a song about her.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Mary Ann.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Mary Ann. He wrote a song about her.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So you and dad and Mary Ann drove out to L.A. Dad wanted to be in L.A., and ten . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah. So all he wanted – I realized after he got there, what he wanted was to interfere with my affairs, my business. Then when he couldn’t, “I want to go home, boy.” Kept nagging about going home. I said, “Wait a minute, Dad. I’ve got business to take care of out here. Let me take care of my business.” “No, boy. When you taking me

home?” Like that. He kept on. I told Mary Ann. I said, “Mary Ann, I’m going to do something you don’t like, but I got to do it for peace, to have a little peace.” I said, “I’m going to take my father home.”

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: This is, to me, one of the most interesting parts of your life – though every part of your life is interesting to me – but one of the most interesting parts of your life is that here you’re out in California under the auspices of Ray Charles, who has become your mentor. You’ve cut an album he loves. Whether it’s released or not is another story. Ray artistically loved the album . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yes he did.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . because he told that to me and many other people. And he loved your style of singing. Ray had never produced another vocalist before. This was a big thing. He only produced his own stuff. So, okay, the album’s done. He produced a vocalist he loved. You’re in California, land of opportunity. Dad, who abandoned you as a child and never kept everybody together after mom died, is telling you, “Boy, drive me back home.” So my question to you – it doesn’t have any real answer, but I love hearing you talk, so I’ll be happy to hear you tell me whatever you tell me: why didn’t you tell him, “Dad, I’m in California. Take the bus home.”

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I did. I said, “Look here. I’m out here. This is where my business generates.”

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Right. So he prevailed upon you.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: He got to go home. I said – kept on, and then I thought, I’m going to take this man home. So the first break I got where I would have the time to drive him home and come back myself, I did. When I came back . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: To Cleveland.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: When I came back from Cleveland to California, Mary Ann had an attitude about me taking him home. All of a sudden . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: It turned bad.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah. She was going to leave. We had adopted a little boy, who is now – Tracy’s now about 46 – something like that, because when came back and I found out he was still alive – he’s now – he’s got a job being a x-ray technician.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Right. I talked to him. He lives in Tennessee, right?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Uh-huh.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Kentucky? Kentucky.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Oh yeah. And looks good.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Nice guy.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Nice kid. I . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So when you got back to California, things weren’t happening, and then you went back to Cleveland.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Right. So she jumped up and grabs the kid and leaves. I don’t know where neither of them was. Anyhow, I’m out there, and I decided, might as well go back . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: To Cleveland.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . to Cleveland.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Jimmy, before we go back to Cleveland and trace the end of the decade, let me, before I forget, because the story I love so much, I want to get that on tape – the time you played with Charlie Parker.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Oh yeah.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Now you had met Bird . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: That was before . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Exactly. No, this is 1950s, the mid- . . ..

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah. Early 1950s. Yeah, because what? – he died in like ’52 or something like that.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: He died in ’55, I think.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: It was something like that. Yeah.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: The early 1950s. I just want to hear on tape – I just don’t have it on tape – how you two performed together.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: We all – we’d finish our gigs and hurry up and go down to Birdland. That was our hangout after we did our shows around New York and New Jersey and whatever.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Birdland was our hangout. We would all get together and go down there and jam with Bird. One night I came down, and as I came down the step, he was playing Embraceable You. He saw me, and he knew I knew it – the song. Motioned for me to come on up. Come on up here. So I went up to the stage. He said, “You take the next chorus.” I got up, and I sang Embraceable You with him.” But I didn’t know that Columbia was going to record it. They recorded. It is on one of his old albums. That sort of upset me, because nobody had offered me anything to release it to the public. But, that’s the kind of thing that they pulled.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Okay, so getting back into the time zone here. 1960s, ’3, ’4, you go back to Cleveland. What kind of jobs did you do in that period before you got this call from Joel Dorn to do . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I was a busboy in restaurants. In the train station, there was a restaurant called Fred Harvey’s.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Oh yeah. It was a chain back then.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: They had a chain in various stations and various big buildings – business buildings, whatnot. I worked for them. I worked for other restaurants.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Was it with humility that you worked?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Huh?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Did you work with anger and bitterness, to a degree?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: In a way, I did have an inner anger . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: An inner anger.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . because I didn’t want to do that. I wanted to work with my career. I didn’t have an agent, so how was I going to work? The agent I had, he wasn’t doing anything to support my career, but he was taking the money that was offered for my engagements. That was Jimmy Evans.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Jimmy Evans, a famous guy, at the time.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: He also destroyed poor Maybelle. I hated it when I found out he had her as an artist, too. That was the worst thing, for her to have him and nobody there to protect her or handle her business for her. There was nothing I could do, because I didn’t have anyone to handle mine. So obviously, I had to back off from her situation and try to deal with my own. That was what was happening. I had to have a place to live, and of course

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: if you’ve got to live, you got to pay rent. So I had to get a place, an apartment, small [?]. Two or three rooms, I think I had – three-room apartment, because I had a brother that came and lived with me.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Kenny lived with you?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Kenny – Kenneth. But he was hardheaded and wouldn’t listen. So I had to let him go his own way. That was a little struggle, because – I don’t say it was a big struggle, because I had been by myself so long over the years, it didn’t bother me, being by myself and taking care of myself. It didn’t bother me at all. No. It never became a thing with me.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Where were you – I know you were in Cleveland – but when you get this call in 1968 or 1969 from Joel Dorn, who’s a producer at Atlantic, how did that all come about?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Joel Dorn?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah. The Source, I’m talking about. The album that became The Source.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: That was a problem. He was with Atlantic.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Right.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: That was the problems of being my agent. It didn’t work out, because he did nothing. I’m wondering, all these people are getting advertisements about their career and who they are and whatnot, but I never got any and there was never any to support my career. So I just had to wonder about it and let it go.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: But when you were hired by Atlantic, when you were signed to Atlantic, at least for this one album that Joel Dorn was producing, the album on which you sing Day by Day and the song from Exodus and On Broadway – tell me about the experience of making that album. Because that’s really – between Falling in Love is Wonderful, which is the name of the Ray Charles album, done in the early ’60s, and The Source, which is done in the late ’60s – this is really the next great Jimmy Scott that we all know will live forever.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: That was actually the first great album that I got through, as far as the music and the arrangements and the selection of tunes.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: That’s what I wanted to ask you about. Did Joel give you the freedom to pick songs?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yes, yes. Why, I don’t know, because after that, he was like all the rest of them. He didn’t – and I’m wondering, what is this cat doing?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So in other words, you didn’t feel as though, once the album was done, it wasn’t promoted with . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: That’s right.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . the enthusiasm or promoted . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: It wasn’t promoted properly. That was another thing with Lubinsky and all of them that I had made records for before. They didn’t promote anything. The records are out there, even now.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: When The Source came out, and there was a picture of a woman on the cover, did that anger you?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: The . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: The Source.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: The Source? A black girl?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah, on Atlantic. She had a big afro.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah. Somewhat, because that wasn’t – to me, that wasn’t selling me as an artist. Here’s someone else on it, and it looked like they were saying she did this album. She didn’t do the album. I did the album. Boy. I done been through hell.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: 1971, you’re working in Cleveland at the hotel. Tell us about that accident you had, because that had a big impact on your life.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I was shipping and receiving clerk for the hotel. So food comes in, I have to accept it for the hotel. Packages come in, I have to accept it for the hotel. But some of the things weren’t just for the hotel. They were for people who resided there as well. Someone would send a package to somebody that had a room there at the hotel and was staying there a long while. Packages came to them. When they came, I had to deliver them to their rooms in the hotel. When the accident happened, that day a shipment of food supplies came in. I got the skid – I had a skid down there – and I stacked them on the skid. I took them down to the little store, because he worked with me, that fellow that had the little store. He worked with me. I would have to take food or anything like that – that would go to him. I didn’t know he had made this shipment. He didn’t say to me, “Scott, I got a shipment coming in” or nothing like that.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: It came in. I loaded it on the skid. I got it down to the little store in the hotel. He said, “No, no, no. We can’t put it in here” in the little store. He didn’t have any room for it. But, the guy had planned to put it in another room which they used for storage. It was on the thirteenth floor. Now I had to pull this skid into the elevator with the stack of food and stuff on it – canned food and stuff like that. When I got up to the thirteenth floor, this guy goes in front of me and says, “Just a minute.” Opens this door, and this room is like – okay, the elevator door opens, and there’s the room where – it wasn’t a distance, a long distance or anything. The thing is, when I got there – in there – the guy says – showed me where he wanted me to put it. It was between some other boxes and some other platforms. So they said, “Put the skid there, and I’ll have Johnson stack it tomorrow.” I said, “Okay.” I tried to back it in there. When I tried to back it in there, I got my foot caught in the thing, and I turned around and fell backwards.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: You fell backwards.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: That’s when all the injuries . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: All the injuries start. So you had.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . started.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I always look at that both kind of literal and metaphorical. Things kind of went downhill from there, and you have this long period from ’73-ish until ’84 where you’re living in Cleveland. You’re not doing much. You’ve had this accident. Your hips are really . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No. I didn’t have a job . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: You didn’t have a job.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . or anything like that.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: You worked at old age homes. But then, in ’84, an interesting thing happens. Freddy Mendelsohn calls you. By now, Lubinsky’s gone. ’84. Jeannie Scott: ’74.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah, oh, that’s what I meant to say: ’74. Lubinsky – Freddy Mendelsohn calls you in 1974, and he tells you he wants you to do an album – another album for Savoy, Can’t We Begin Again?, which has all sorts of hopeful implications. Tell me about that album. Jimmy Scott: I don’t know. I never saw any publicity on it, and I hardly heard it on the radio. That’s the way they worked.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: But he gave you some money for that, didn’t he, or not?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Who?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Mendelsohn. Freddy Mendelsohn.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Mendelsohn, yeah.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Because I got the idea that he wanted to a degree [to] make up . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I think it was $10,000.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Which is a whole lot more than you ever got from . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Whole lot more than Lubinsky would have gave. The best I’d have got out of Lubinsky is $5,000.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I guess the other powerful thing that happens in that period, in the mid-1970s, when you’ve done this album, Can’t We Begin Again?, is the thing that happens on the jazz station in Newark, where somebody says . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah. Bill Cook was the deejay for that. Bill Cook had a club in Newark. It was a jazz club. Everybody hung out there at Bill Cook’s place, and everybody knew he was a deejay and had the radio show. Bill Cook was, at one time, pretty big there in Newark. But he did nothing with it. He had a lot of opportunities, but he didn’t do anything with it. He had everybody available that would help him, or be on his shows to help him. No. Didn’t happen.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: But I’m talking about that time that they put you on the radio in Newark, because somebody had called in and said, “Jimmy Scott’s dead,” because you were always loved in Newark, because you kind of began in Newark, to a certain degree. Newark was the town where you had really made your mark. When you had heard somebody . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: In a way, that was my town.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Right, Newark was your town in a certain way.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: In those days.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Because guys like Joe Pesci and Frankie Vallee, they all . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Joe Pesci and them came over then. Frankie Vallee, he used to come over with Joe Pesci and hang out and try to get me to sing songs with him.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Because they idolized you, and they loved your style. They wanted to copy your style. But what I was moving towards, that time when you get on the radio, and you’re telling people, no, I’m not dead; I’m alive and well. Then, suddenly, the calls start coming in, and you’re there all day. People are remembering and going, wow, Jimmy Scott’s not only now alive – tell us about that day that they had you on the radio.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: There was all kinds of people that called – agents, club owners, and like that. I am just so disgusted that I didn’t have someone to keep a record of who those people were, because, see there, I would have had a lot of work. I was offered a lot of work that day. So, it was a good day in that sense, but nothing ever came of it, because I didn’t have anybody who could handle business books.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah, but you did play Newark after that.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Oh yeah.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: And you did move back to Newark and reignite your career to a degree.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Right, because I used to work Newark and Long Island – out Long Island, and New York – the Baby Grands, both of them. One was in Harlem and the other one was in Brooklyn on Nostrand and Bedford, on the corner. Both of them were established on the corner of the street, like Nostrand was going through – one Baby Grand [?] on Nostrand. Then the other was 125th. It was on 125th . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: The Baby Grand up in Harlem.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . yeah, and Eighth Avenue.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: On that day, Jimmy, in Newark, when people started calling, like Quincy Jones or whoever – I think a lot of people called – and it all began because it was reported on the radio that you were dead. Here you are talking on the radio. You come down to the station. You get some gigs. Did it renew your spirit?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yes, it helped a lot. It helped a lot.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: It helped to renew your spirit. Then another part of your career begins, where you’re playing little clubs, like the Baby Grand, like you were saying, in Long Island and all over, but you’re still struggling, but you’re able to make a humble living as a jazz singer. Is that accurate?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No. It wasn’t enough. I wasn’t able to make a steady living . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Ah. That’s the distinction that has to be made.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . a steady income . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: There was no steady income.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . that would support me until things got in shape or I could find someone who could handle things for me. I had a sister who lived there, but they never – none of my folks ever wanted to be around me. I have never had any of them at a performance of mine. No-one in the family. What are you going to do? So I couldn’t talk to them about the business end, because they had to come around.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Do you know – tell me about – because this is an important character in the new phase of your career – tell me when you first met Doc Pomus, the great . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: At the Baby Grand. The funniest thing, he had a metal brace . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: On his leg.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . on his leg.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: This is Doc Pomus, the great blues composer and singer.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Right, and writer. Anyway, Doc used to come to the Baby Grand.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: This is in the late 1940s.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Anyhow, he was sitting in the chair, and this brace was reflecting light. He would move his foot or something, and the lights would reflect. I kept seeing this. Then I realized, that’s that thing on his leg. That’s how we met, because when I’d come off, I knew who he was. I go over and greet him. We sat and talked and became friends. I even was invited to his house. Ertugun – Nes Ertugun – it wasn’t Ertugun – his brother? What is it?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Raoul.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Raoul, yeah.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Felder.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Oh boy. He didn’t like it, because . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: The lawyer.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . yeah. He didn’t like it, because Doc Pomus brought me to his house, and I had dinner with him. He didn’t like it. Very nasty.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: The record industry, for not giving Jimmy Scott a record deal. He says, “What’s wrong with you guys? This is one of the greatest vocalists there is out there. Why don’t you give him a deal? This is crazy. He is going to die, and everybody’s going to say how great he was, and he’ll never have a deal.” Tell me your reaction. Did you read that letter in Billboard? Or did you learn about it?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No, I didn’t.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So you didn’t even know that it happened.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No, I didn’t.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Because you weren’t even reading Billboard then. Neither was I.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: He would call my house. Keep up with me. “How you doing, Jim?” I said, “Good.” Until the end. That last call I got, the person that called told me he passed.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Now we’re in the early ’90s. When you were invited to perform at Doc’s funeral, you had no hesitancy.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: You were going to do it.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I did it.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Tell me about that funeral.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: It was highly sad in many ways, and a lot of people felt that sadness.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Do you remember what song you sang?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Uh . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Somebody to Watch over Me, wasn’t it?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Someone to Watch over Me. You’re right.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Tell us what happened after the funeral.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Huh?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Tell us what happened after the funeral.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Everybody went their own way. I got on the train and went back to Newark, because I was living in Newark at the time. I had an apartment there. I went on back to Newark.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: When was the first time that you heard, as a result of your performance at the funeral, there was interest in you as a recording artist again?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Interest?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I’ll ask it again. When was the first time, after the funeral, you heard that there was interest in you as a recording artist – that people were beginning to talk about recording you, because they had heard you do Somebody to Watch over Me at the funeral? When did that happen? Who called you?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: It was a little reporter that lived in Brooklyn. He called and told me what was going on.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Then did you hear from Seymour Stein? Did he call you? Or you don’t recall that?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I don’t recall.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Because what I’m trying to figure out is how – what led to making the album All the Way with Tommy LiPuma?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Actually, the attention came from the funeral. The attention came from the funeral, and they got together and got him. I think he did a good job for the recording, helping to produce the recording. I think Tommy did a good job.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Did you think – was all this taking you by surprise? Because it had been so long since you had had a record deal. To get a recording contract from Warner Bros. Records, which is a huge label, as a result of singing at the funeral and having Seymour Stein – who was a big-shot music mogul – hear you and able to give you a contract, and then give you one of the leading jazz producers in the country, must have been a big thrill? Or were you excited?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: It was for me, yeah.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: You were excited by that.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: You get excited . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: But you’re scared it . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . and you always hope that this is it.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Right. That’s what I’m saying. But you had been excited before and been disappointed, so you . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yes.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . you keep your expectations down.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: There you go. You’re fighting to keep from getting excited over things.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Knowing that your heart might be broken, and you don’t want to deal with another broken heart.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah, right. So many times.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So many times. So many times.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: You’ve got the idea. You’re right dead-on the idea.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: You want to keep your expectations down, because you don’t want your heart broken again.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Right.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Tell about – again, the – when, in picking out the tunes and all, was that a happy experience? Were you involved artistically in the making of that album?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yes.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So nobody imposed material on you that you don’t want to do.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No. We created the songs, myself and Tommy, with his suggestions and his ideas. He put it over beautifully. I got to give it to him.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: As a result, in the ’90s you were able to find some work and be rediscovered by a group of people, one of whom was Lou Reed. How did you meet Lou Reed?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: They were coming to the club.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I think Doc was friends with Lou.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah. They’d come over to see Doc and hang with him. That was because Doc was a writer. Lou liked his work and would try get Doc to write songs for him. I think Doc gave it up and never did another tune for him.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: When Lou asked you to tour with him – was that a surprise for you, when Lou Reed . . .?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah. I’m – what is this?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: What is this?! Did you even know what his music was like?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: See, Lou is gay, and he wanted to mess around. That wasn’t my thing. I wasn’t into that crap. Okay? I knew many that were, but no, not me. No. So I had to tell him, take it another way, because it ain’t here. This ain’t the stuff.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: What was the music like on that tour, going to England and Europe? How was your music received? Or did you sing his music?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Beautiful. I think he got jealous, because of the response that I got from the audience. He began acting funny.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Haughty?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So I said, oh, well, okay, because I’ve seen it before. It wasn’t like I hadn’t seen that before. So I went on about my business, and Lou went on about his. But Lou still tries to come around and make me think like he thinks. It’ll never happen. It hasn’t happened all these years. So it’ll never happen, baby. No, baby, they can take that gay mess and keep it to themselves. God bless ’em.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: So you come back after being on the road with Lou. Then, this is also this period of time when you get a lot of national exposure, isn’t it? – when you appear in the David Byrne television show.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yes.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: What’s that called again?
Jeannie Scott: [inaudible]

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Sessions at 54 – no, but I was thinking about the t.v. show, that big-time t.v. show. Jimmy Scott: Oh yeah. He had a different name for the t.v. show.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah. You know, the famous show. It was a cult t.v. show. He was on the final episode. Jeannie Scott: “Twin Peaks.”

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah, “Twin Peaks,” because that always killed me. Jeannie Scott: That’s David Lynch.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I mean David Lynch. Forgive me. David Byrne . . . Jimmy Scott: What was the name of it?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: David Lynch, the director. It’s my mind turning to mush. David Lynch, who had you on the episode, the concluding episode of “Twin Peaks.” What was that like? How did that come about?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I was accepted quite well and supported beautifully with the band. Then they had me come in and do something with strings – with the band, but strings were added. I don’t know what they ever did with those records.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Oh yeah. It would be good to have them, because they never came out.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Then you have this long – or at least three- or four-, five-years period where you get a recording contract with Fantasy and you do these albums produced by . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah. That was . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Todd Barkin.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: . . . Todd Barkin. Yeah.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Tell us about those albums and . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Todd was skunky too. He was one of them skunks that they didn’t want to do right and you were supposed to accept it, because they were who they were.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Because – but your feeling about that was that they didn’t give you the artistic freedom, they didn’t let you pick the . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: They didn’t respect you.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I see.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: They didn’t respect your ability. Everything turned out to be nothing.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: On the personal tip here – one thing I’d like to get in here, because we haven’t talked about the various women: Angel, Chaney, Ruth. A lot of women in your life, and a lot of lovely women, a lot of difficult women. Overall – and of course I want to hear the Jeannie story for the tape – but overall, how would you characterize your relationship with women?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: With who?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Women, in general.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: It was . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Jimmy and women.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I’ll tell you. The women, they were hungry.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: They were hungry, he says.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Yeah, and all they wanted was, “You’re an entertainer, you’re making money, and give it to me.” Naturally most of them felt – the ones that I went out with, that’s the way most of them felt. I didn’t feel that that was what I wanted for life, so we didn’t get along. I just went ahead and lived my life. But the only women I’ve ever had that has shown me what a wife is is this young lady right here.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Jeannie.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Jeannie.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: How did you meet Jeannie?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: I was at – was it? – the Birdland on 52nd, when they moved from the other place. I was there. Jeannie and a friend of hers and mine came into Birdland at night, that I was there. I was introduced to Jeannie. What’s Steve’s last name?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Steve Nicholas.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Nichols?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: However. He introduced me to Jeannie. That was it. It was over, because I dug her attitude first and how she was such a lady about – she’s out there in the streets with us, but she was a lady and acted that way. That’s what I respected about her.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: You – in your mind, you had never had another woman who cared about helping you with your career.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Not one of them.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No. Not any at all.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Not Catherine or Francis or Chaney or Eve or . . .

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: First – this is the first woman that ever took it upon herself to find out information, bring it to me. We’d discuss it. If it was good, she’d work on it for me. We’ve been successful in our relationship because of that, I feel. Right, Jeannie?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Let me ask you some general questions about the jazz life, that you’ve lived the jazz life your whole life.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: Who?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: The jazz life, by which I mean, you’re making it up as you go along. The jazz life is not – you’ve never lived a conventional life.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: No.

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Ritz
Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.text: You’ve always lived an unconventional life. Do you feel that you’ve been true to your art?

Jimmy_Scott_SI-NEA_oral_history new logo.speaker: Scott
